newsitem.title: UK: J.Bibby agrees takeover by Barlow.
newsitem.headline: J.Bibby agrees takeover by Barlow.

text.p: British diversified industrials and trading group J. Bibby & Sons Plc has agreed to become a wholly-owned subsidiary of South Africa's Barlow Ltd, the companies said on Tuesday in a joint statement.

Under the proposal Bibby minority shareholders will receive 195 pence for each Bibby share, of which five pence will be by way of a special dividend and the balance paid by Barlow UK Investments Plc, a unit of Barlow Ltd. The price represents a premium of 52 percent to the share price of 128.5 pence on the day before the discussions started.
The proposal values Bibby at around 315 million stg and the minority shares -- some 23.8 percent of Bibby's fully diluted share capital -- at about 70 million stg.
Barlow currently owns some 78.8 percent of Bibby.
The agreement is subject to approval by Bibby's minority shareholders, who are expected to meet in May. The scheme is expected to become effective by the end of June.
"We are pleased that agreement has been reached on the best way forward for both companies," said John Thomson, vice-chairman and independent director of Biddy.
"Full integration of the Bibby business within the Barlow group will result in a stronger force in the markets in which they operate".
Robert Fleming & Co Ltd acted for Bibby and Standard Bank London Ltd for Barlow.
Bibby shares stood at an unchanged 188 pence at 0900 GMT.
